identification.name: Invar 36 Alloy (Cold Drawn)
identification.common_form_notes: Typically sourced as cold drawn bar stock. Invar 36® is a registered trademark of Carpenter Technology Corporation.
identification.notes: 36% nickel-iron alloy with a coefficient of thermal expansion approximately one-tenth that of carbon steel up to ~190°C (thermal inflection point where the low-CTE Invar effect begins to break down). Curie temperature 279°C — above this, ferromagnetic properties are lost. Also known as Nilo 36, FeNi36, and Invar M93. Equivalent designations: UNS K93600 (annealed), UNS K93601 (cold drawn); W. Nr. 1.3912; ASTM B753 Alloy T36. Machinability similar to AISI 304 stainless steel. Can be welded, brazed, and plated. Young's modulus varies with temper: MatWeb reports 148 GPa for cold drawn bar; SpaceMatDB reports 140 GPa (temper unspecified). Qualified for space applications; stress corrosion cracking resistance tested per ECSS-Q-ST-70-36C. Data primarily from Carpenter Technology Corporation (MatWeb) with supplemental data from SpaceMatDB.

typical_usage: Applications requiring minimal dimensional change with temperature: precision optical and laser systems, aircraft controls, radio and electronic devices, bimetallic thermostats, rod-and-tube temperature regulators, space structures and instrument frames. The extremely low CTE near room temperature is its primary design advantage.
